title: Quality and Reliability Engineer
description: Headquarters: URL: http://cmswa.com Custom Mechanical Solutions delivers energy-efficient HVAC systems across the Pacific Northwest, with deep expertise in healthcare, education, data centers, and retrofit projects. We work with top manufacturers to meet performance and sustainability goals—always focused on quality, care, and progress. If you're ready to grow your career, we’re glad you found us. At CMS, you’ll join a team that supports your development and gives you space to make an impact.  We review every application carefully and appreciate your interest in growing your career with our team. About Custom Mechanical Solutions Custom Mechanical Solutions (CMS) provides commercial HVAC equipment and technical solutions for complex building applications. We partner with contractors, engineers, building owners, and manufacturers throughout the equipment lifecycle—from system design and delivery through startup, troubleshooting, and field support. As part of the Meriton family of companies, CMS maintains its specialized technical expertise and customer-focused approach while benefiting from the resources and long-term investment of a growing national organization. Title: Quality & Reliability Engineer Department: CMS National Accounts Location: Fully remote within the United States Travel: Approximately 10–20% domestic and international travel Turn field challenges into better products, stronger processes, and more reliable outcomes. Join a growing National Accounts team where your technical judgment, curiosity, and follow-through will connect the jobsite to the factory and help shape how quality is managed as the business scales. The opportunity CMS is looking for a Quality & Reliability Engineer to own and continuously improve the field-to-factory quality feedback loop for custom commercial and industrial HVAC equipment. You will lead technical investigations, turn incomplete field information into clear problem statements, and keep root-cause and corrective-action work moving through verified closure. This is a hands-on, highly collaborative role. You will work across field operations, project teams, customers, engineering, manufacturing, suppliers, and factory quality leaders. Your work will help teams respond faster, create repeatable repairs, reduce recurrence, and apply lessons learned to future projects. Work from where you are. This is a fully remote position that can be based anywhere within the United States. Approximately 10-20% domestic and international travel is expected, including travel to customer sites and manufacturing facilities in Mexico. Travel may be heavier initially while you build relationships with key stakeholders and learn the factory systems. Travel to Mexico is generally expected up to four times per year to support investigations, gather technical evidence, collaborate with factory teams, and validate corrective actions. What you will own Lead field-to-factory investigations. Coordinate quality issues from initial report through containment, root cause, corrective action, and verified closure. Turn field intelligence into action. Gather the technical evidence needed for faster decisions and translate recurring trends into improvements in design, manufacturing, supplier controls, installation guidance, training, and documentation. Create field-ready solutions. Develop clear, controlled Field Service Bulletins with approved repair steps, safety requirements, acceptance criteria, and closeout evidence. Drive clarity and accountability. Keep owners, milestones, risks, decisions, and overdue actions visible. Remove blockers and escalate high-impact or aging issues when needed. Use data to improve the program. Maintain quality dashboards and reports, identify systemic trends and emerging risks, and provide concise updates to leadership, project teams, customers, and factory partners. Go where the evidence is. Travel to customer sites and manufacturing facilities in Mexico to inspect equipment, support troubleshooting, gather evidence, collaborate with factory teams, and validate repair effectiveness. You will probably love this role if... When something fails, your first question is “Why?” and you keep digging until the evidence supports the answer. You enjoy both the technical details and the bigger picture, from walking a jobsite and troubleshooting equipment to explaining the path forward clearly. You take ownership without waiting for every step to be laid out, bring the right people together, and keep work moving until the issue is truly closed. You are comfortable influencing across teams, even when you do not directly manage the people involved. You want to help build and improve a quality program, not simply maintain one. Required qualifications A bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Manufacturing, or Quality Engineering, or an equivalent combination of technical education and relevant professional experience. At least three years of relevant experience in manufacturing quality, field service, commissioning, reliability engineering, technical investigations, or related technical project support. Strong mechanical and/or electrical investigation and troubleshooting skills. Working knowledge of structured problem-solving methods such as RCA, CAPA, 8D, 5 Why, fishbone analysis, or FMEA. Ability to translate incomplete field information into clear technical problem statements and drive corrective actions through verified closure. Ability to communicate complex technical issues clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences. Ability to travel domestically and internationally approximately 10–20%, including travel to manufacturing facilities in Mexico. A valid passport at the time of hire is preferred; candidates without one must be able to obtain one within the first 90 days of employment. Preferred qualifications Five or more years of relevant quality, reliability, field-service, commissioning, or technical investigation experience. Direct experience with commercial or industrial HVAC equipment. Experience with custom air-handling equipment, controls, construction drawings and specifications, startup, commissioning, or active job-site processes. Experience working directly with manufacturing facilities, suppliers, factory quality teams, or field-service organizations. Experience developing technical repair procedures, Field Service Bulletins, corrective-action documentation, or quality dashboards. Compensation and benefits Base salary: $95,000-$125,000 annually, depending on experience. This position is also eligible for a discretionary bonus. Eligible employees may participate in Meriton’s benefits programs in accordance with applicable plan terms. Why CMS National Accounts You will join a fast-moving team supporting complex equipment and significant projects where expectations are high, and the connection between field performance and customer experience matters. This role offers the opportunity to make quality information more complete, corrective actions more durable, repairs more repeatable, and lessons learned more useful across a growing portfolio. If you are ready to solve meaningful technical problems and help build a stronger quality and reliability program, we would like to hear from you. Custom Mechanical Solutions is an Equal Opportunity Employer Employment practices will not be influenced or affected by an applicant’s or employee’s race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status or any other legally protected status.  Reasonable accommodations will be made for qualified individuals with disabilities unless doing so would result in an undue hardship. title: Principal Product Management, Growth
description: Headquarters: Remote ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You’ll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won’t just contribute. You’ll make things happen fast. Principal Product Manager, Growth About ZoomInfo ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You'll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won't just contribute — you'll make things happen, fast. The Opportunity Own a Growth Portfolio and Set the Pattern the Rest of the Team Inherits ZoomInfo built the industry's most sophisticated GTM data platform. The next frontier is turning every visitor into revenue without waiting on a human handoff — a coherent self-serve journey that activates a non-customer in minutes, converts consumption into upgrade, and routes high-intent signals back to sales when a human will close more than they distract. You'll define the multi-quarter thesis on which channels compound, the operating rhythm the rest of the growth PM team inherits, and the ZoomInfo POV on how buyers discover us in an AI-first world. The impact is immediate and compounding. Every signup you activate, every credit you cause to be consumed, every transaction, every PQL you route, every "buy more" event you trigger is revenue — and every operating pattern you set multiplies across the growth PM group. We've adopted a consumption-first monetization model and a unified entry-point thesis across the company, and we run weekly: if your hypothesis can't be falsified inside a sprint, it isn't a hypothesis. This is a rare opportunity to own a P&L-shaped surface with full air cover to ship fast, learn in public, re-pivot when the data turns — and to define the growth PM craft as ZoomInfo scales it. What You'll Do Own the Portfolio End-to-End Take a portfolio-scope growth surface — and own it from first impression to revenue. Define the entry points, the activation milestones, the monetization moments, and the sales-assist signals across the channels that make up the portfolio. Drive the user experience across surfaces: landing, signup, in-product onboarding, empty states, upgrade modals, paywalls, lifecycle communication, and the agent-readable / LLM-discovery surfaces that are becoming primary. You own the funnel chart; you own the why behind every drop. Set the Multi-Quarter Growth Thesis Beyond weekly experiments, own 4-8 quarter bets on which channels compound and which retire. Publish a written POV on where PLG distribution is heading (LLM-first discovery, MCP-as-channel, agent-readable onboarding, partner-driven trials) and defend the sequencing to the exec team. Rebalance investment across the portfolio quarterly based on unit economics, not the loudest channel. Run Experimentation as the Operating Rhythm — and Set the Rhythm for the Team Ship 8-10 experiments per sprint. Pre-register the hypothesis, the metric, the success threshold, and — critically — the invalidation signal. Read results weekly, kill what doesn't work, double down on what does, and keep a written record so the team compounds learning instead of repeating it. Your rubric, your retro format, and your invalidation-signal standard become the template the rest of the Growth PM group inherits. Translate results into concrete changes: copy rewrites, schema tweaks, pricing changes, new flows, retired ones. Close the loop with engineering, design, and analytics inside the same week. Design Self-Serve as a First-Class Path Most users on your portfolio never speak to sales before they hit a "buy more" moment. Your in-product copy, paywall framing, empty states, activation paths, and upgrade triggers are the product. Apply growth-engineering rigor — credit economics, consumption pacing, signal routing, lifecycle messaging, intelligent gating — so the right offer lands in front of the right user at exactly the right moment. Hand high-intent users to sales with a clean signal; absorb low-intent users with a clean self-serve path. Diagnose the Funnel With Data, Not Vibes Data is your default tool, not a thing you ask analytics to do for you. You independently analyze the funnel, segment the cohort, find the leak, and propose the fix — then validate it with an experiment. You know when to trust a 5% lift and when to call it noise. Just as important: you know when to zoom out from a specific funnel drop to a portfolio-level rebalance, and can defend that call. Shape the Monetization Mechanic You'll design the credit economics of your portfolio: what's free, what's gated, what gets a "buy more" prompt, what triggers a PQL. You'll model the unit economics — credit cost, revenue per credit, upgrade rate, expansion rate — and you'll defend the pricing decisions in front of finance and sales leadership with the math. Orchestrate Across Sales, Marketing, and CS Self-serve doesn't mean alone. You'll route PQLs into the right hands (AE, SC, AM, or no one), partner with marketing on acquisition and lifecycle, and work with CS to understand why activated users churn before upgrade. You'll run the operating cadences that keep your portfolio aligned with the broader PLG portfolio without becoming a meeting machine. Multiply the Team Help hire and calibrate the Sr Growth PMs owning adjacent loops. Coach them into ownership. Your retro is their template; your experiment quality is their bar. Raise the craft of the whole Growth PM group as it scales. Stay Honest About What's Working Write retrospectives that name the wrong calls as cleanly as the right ones. Update your priors publicly when the data turns. Hold strong opinions weakly. The team that ships the most experiments isn't the team that's right the most — it's the team that updates the fastest. What You'll Bring 8–12 years of product management experience, with 4+ years specifically in growth, PLG, or self-serve product roles Direct P&L ownership at portfolio scope — a loop or portfolio you've driven from <$X to >$Y with your name on the number, not a feature inside someone else's loop Experience presenting to CEO / CRO / CFO / board on growth mechanics — the credit-economics deck, the funnel narrative, the "kill this bet" moment Track record of hiring, mentoring, or calibrating other growth PMs — comfortable being the bar You're a builder. You ship landing pages, signup flows, and in-product experiments — not specs that sit in Jira. You sit with designers and engineers, write copy, and prototype with code. AI-fluent with a public POV. You understand that LLMs are becoming a primary discovery surface. You have opinions — publishable ones — about agent-readable flows, MCP-as-distribution, GEO/AEO, and how an AI agent's recommendation impacts a funnel. Marketing-fluent. You hold your own with SEO, paid acquisition, content, and lifecycle marketing teams as a peer, not a consumer. Demonstrated track record of running structured experimentation (A/B tests, multivariate, holdouts, pre/post) at sprint cadence — including at cohort sizes where 50/50 doesn't have power Strong analytics fluency — comfortable in Snowflake without analyst hand-holding Working knowledge of consumption-based pricing, credit economics, freemium mechanics, and PQL frameworks B2B SaaS background; data, GTM, or sales-tech domain experience is a plus but not required Who You Are Core Competencies Funnel Foundation. Expert-level understanding of full-funnel growth. You can reason about activation rates, time-to-value, retention curves, credit economics, upgrade triggers, and PQL signal quality with depth. You've owned a growth loop — or portfolio — in production. SQL and analytics fluency let you diagnose a funnel drop, prototype the fix, and validate it in the same week. Portfolio Thinking. You reason about ToF (or an equivalent surface) as a portfolio of channels with different unit economics, decay curves, and compounding dynamics — not a single funnel. You rebalance investment quarterly based on where marginal dollars return the most, and you can defend the rebalance to leadership with the math. Experimentation Discipline. You don't ship without a hypothesis. You pre-register the metric and the invalidation signal before the test runs. You read results honestly, kill losing variants without ego, and document learnings so the team compounds knowledge instead of relitigating settled questions. You know the difference between an experiment and a launch — and you can tell when each is the right move. Category POV. You have a public, defensible point of view on where PLG distribution is heading — agent-readable surfaces, MCP-as-channel, GEO/AEO, LLM-first onboarding — grounded in benchmarks from peer companies (Clay, Linear, Vercel, Cursor, Notion), not just internal data. That POV shows up in the roadmap. Distribution Mindset. Experience designing growth surfaces where sales teams, marketing teams, and self-serve users are simultaneously your customers. You measure success through revenue, consumption, and expansion velocity, not screens shipped. You understand growth economics: each additional entry point, freemium offer, or AI trial compounds in value through shared activation patterns, amortized acquisition costs, and recurring consumption network effects. Operational Velocity. You read the funnel daily, not quarterly. You prototype emerging mechanics — paywalls, in-app prompts, lifecycle sequences — to understand their practical constraints before committing engineering time. You hold strong opinions weakly, updating your design assumptions as evidence accumulates, publicly, even when the prior thesis was your own. Strategic Communication. You translate between funnel depth and business impact fluently. You can explain to the CEO why a credit pricing change is worth a quarter of work. You can communicate to engineers why a revenue constraint requires a "quiet release" in two weeks rather than a polished launch in three months. You influence without formal authority through forcing functions, falsifiable invalidation signals, and earned credibility. Talent Leverage. You coach Sr PMs into full ownership of their loops. Your retro is their template. Your experiment quality is their bar. You help hire the next PMs on the team, and you calibrate — you know what "great" looks like at Sr level and you can articulate the gap to someone who isn't there yet. Copy Instinct. Microcopy is part of your craft, not someone else's job. You can rewrite a paywall headline, an upgrade modal, an empty state, or an onboarding CTA on instinct — and defend the rewrite with PLG principles. You know when to ask content design for help and when to ship the rewrite yourself. The Environment Reporting, Pace & Impact Reporting & Collaboration. Report to the VP Product, PLG. Peer to the Sr Directors of Marketing, Sales Operations, and Customer Success on the growth contracts (PQL routing, demand-gen alignment, credit economics). Work shoulder-to-shoulder with the engineering and design leaders building the underlying surfaces, the GTM leaders routing PQLs into sales, and a peer PM group covering monetization, lifecycle, viral, onboarding, and analytics. Regular exposure to the CEO, CRO, CMO, and CFO — you own those conversations at your level. Pace & Problems. Fast-moving teams that understand the space. Weekly experimentation cadence layered under 4-quarter portfolio bets. Expect interesting problems: How do we win activation in a user's first 60 seconds? When should two trial flows become one? How do we expose enough value to convert without giving away the platform? How do we price a credit so that customers consume more, not less? When should a self-serve user be routed to sales — and when does that routing actually destroy revenue? How do buyers discover ZoomInfo when discovery goes through Claude and ChatGPT? Your decisions become operating patterns across the PLG organization. Impact. Own a portfolio-scope growth surface at a company that is already AI-first in product thinking and consumption-first in monetization. Your decisions compound. Every improvement to the funnel, the offer, or the activation experience multiplies across multiple products, every partner-driven self-serve channel ZoomInfo ships into, and every AI distribution surface we haven't yet imagined — and every operating pattern you set makes the next PM on the team better. With intelligent borrowing, savings, and budgeting capabilities, Oportun empowers members with the confidence to build a better financial future. Since inception, Oportun has provided more than $22.7 billion in responsible and affordable credit, saved its members more than $2.5 billion in interest and fees, and helped its members set aside an average of more than $1,800 annually. A Quick Note on the Role's Focus While the title is Senior ML Engineer , this opportunity is specifically focused on ML Platform Engineering rather than ML model development or data science. We're looking for engineers with strong software engineering fundamentals and hands-on experience building, scaling, and operating the platforms and infrastructure that enable machine learning in production. The emphasis is on ML infrastructure, MLOps, model serving, platform reliability, and production engineering , rather than primarily developing, training, or fine-tuning ML models. Location Note We’re excited to consider talent currently based in India, as well as candidates who are open to relocating to India for this opportunity. Please note that, as this is a "Remote–India" position, the role must be performed from within India. The Opportunity The Machine Learning Platform team builds the software foundations that enable data scientists and machine learning engineers to develop, validate, deploy, and operate models safely and efficiently in production. In this role, you’ll lead complex platform work from business context through production outcomes, combining hands-on engineering, architectural judgment, production ownership, and mentorship. In your first year, success means leading meaningful platform initiatives, improving reliability and developer experience, and becoming a trusted technical leader for the ML platform. At Oportun, we move fast and hold each other to a high bar. You’ll partner across Data Science, Product, Risk, Fraud, and Engineering to solve ambiguous problems and move the needle for members and the business. What You'll Do Your day-to-day You’ll lead the design, implementation, deployment, and operation of complex platform capabilities that support the machine-learning lifecycle. You’ll design scalable systems for model deployment and serving, feature computation, data validation, workflow orchestration, monitoring, and production support. You’ll build reusable platform components, standards, and automation while improving reliability, scalability, observability, and operational readiness across ML systems. You’ll partner with Data Science, Product, Risk, Fraud, and Engineering teams to translate ambiguous business needs into practical technical solutions. You’ll own significant technical initiatives end to end and lead complex production investigations—clarifying requirements, leading design, delivering safely, measuring results, and implementing durable fixes. You’ll raise engineering quality through thoughtful code and design reviews, mentor engineers through pairing and technical guidance, and contribute to platform technical strategy. You’ll look for ways to use AI tools thoughtfully to work smarter, reduce manual work, and make better decisions faster. Who You Are The right fit looks like this You do not need detailed implementation direction to be effective. Given an ambiguous problem and sufficient context, you can define the technical approach, explain trade-offs, align stakeholders, lead delivery, and own the outcome after launch. You’re comfortable navigating complexity and don’t wait for perfect information to move forward. You communicate clearly, give direct feedback, mentor others, and connect engineering work to member, business, and operational outcomes. What You Bring Skills & experience You’ll have 5+ years of professional software-engineering experience building and operating production systems, with strong programming skills in Python and deep knowledge of API design, distributed systems, service architecture, testing, and software-design fundamentals. You’ve demonstrated experience designing and operating reliable, scalable cloud-native services or data-intensive systems, with experience in ML platforms, model serving, feature engineering, data platforms, MLOps, or related systems. You bring practical experience with SQL, databases, caching, and tracing data or requests across multiple systems, plus familiarity with the ML lifecycle from feature engineering and model training through evaluation, deployment, serving, monitoring, and governance. You have experience with Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, Git-based workflows, and production observability, and you can evaluate technical alternatives and clearly communicate recommendations, trade-offs, risks, and dependencies. You’ve demonstrated the ability to mentor engineers, improve engineering practices, lead through technical influence, and connect engineering work to member, business, product, and operational outcomes. Nice to Have Experience with AWS, Databricks, MLflow, SageMaker, Spark/PySpark, Kafka, or streaming systems. Experience building feature platforms, model-serving systems, workflow-orchestration platforms, or internal developer platforms. Familiarity with monitoring model quality, data quality, feature coverage, latency, reliability, or cost efficiency, and experience working with sensitive data in a regulated or financial-services environment. Experience with Java or another backend language in addition to Python, and familiarity with AI tools such as ChatGPT or Copilot to improve personal productivity. Our AI Mindset We b uild with AI. We lead with judgment. AI isn't a feature here. It's how we work. We're excited about what AI makes possible, and we're looking for people who share that curiosity. You don't need to be an expert. You need to be open to experimenting , willing to learn, and able to apply new tools in ways that actually move the needle. In this role, you'll be encouraged to explore AI tools, find practical use cases for your function, and bring ideas for working smarter. We believe the best outcomes come when human judgment and AI capability work together . Why Oportun What's in it for you Oportun offers a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support your physical, financial, and professional well-being. What you’ll do Implement and iterate on backend features in the Rust-based Knowledge Graph service, including changes to the query engine, SDLC and code indexing flows, and API endpoints (including MCP endpoints) under guidance from senior and staff engineers. Maintain integrations between Knowledge Graph and the rest of the GitLab platform, working in areas that touch GitLab Rails, the Data Insights Platform (Siphon, NATS, ClickHouse), and GitLab Duo Agent Platform. Contribute to system design discussions by proposing options, raising questions, and documenting decisions, with a focus on reliability, scalability, and maintainability for analytical graph workloads. Improve the operational maturity of the service by adding or enhancing metrics, logging, runbooks, alerts, and small readiness tasks, and by participating in on-call rotation as appropriate for your level and experience. Collaborate asynchronously with product, data, infrastructure, security, and AI counterparts to clarify requirements, align on scope, and ship features safely for customers and sustainably for the team. Use AI-assisted development workflows responsibly (for example, using Knowledge Graph-backed agents and internal Duo tooling), and share what works with the team while keeping a strong focus on code quality and correctness. Participate in code reviews, knowledge-sharing sessions, and pairing to both learn from others and help maintain consistent standards across the codebase. Contribute across the stack when needed, including occasional Ruby work for Rails integration and authorization paths, or small frontend changes related to Knowledge Graph features (for example, Software Architecture Map UI plumbing). What you’ll bring Professional experience building and maintaining backend systems in production, with an understanding of reliability, maintainability, and how to support services over time (for example, incident response and follow-ups). Proficiency in at least one modern backend language and strong interest in Rust, with either prior Rust experience or clear evidence you can ramp quickly and deliver in a Rust-first, performance-sensitive codebase. Some exposure to distributed data or analytics systems (for example, OLAP databases, Kafka- or NATS-style messaging, or change data capture (CDC) pipelines), or strong motivation to develop those skills in this role. Interest in graph data modeling and query patterns (property graphs, multi-step (n-hop) traversals, aggregations), and willingness to learn the tools and concepts used in Knowledge Graph over time. Practical experience (or strong interest) using AI tools in day-to-day development, along with a thoughtful approach to validating outputs and integrating AI into your workflow. A language-agnostic mindset and evidence that you can pick up new languages and frameworks as needed (for example, Ruby, Go, or TypeScript/Vue where the work touches adjacent systems). Solid fundamentals in system design for your level, including the ability to reason about trade-offs, ask good questions, and align your implementation work with documented architectural decisions. title: Principal Enterprise Architect

Your proven experience in AWS is the toolkit you use to clear architectural roadblocks and optimize performance, enabling engineering teams to move with unprecedented velocity. As a strategic technical leader who stays close to the code, you inspire an AI-First culture. You bridge the gap between visionary enterprise design and pragmatic execution, driving cross-departmental impact while fostering self-service capabilities and cloud efficiency to ensure that as Jumio grows, our technology scales predictably and elegantly. Key Responsibilities End-to-End System Architecture & Optimization Own the technical vision for scalable, high-performance, cost-efficient systems. Define modern architecture patterns that enable growth, high TPS, and seamless scaling. Architect and optimize multi-tenant SaaS platforms, ensuring configurability and performance. Design self-service capabilities to reduce engineering overhead (e.g., self-service workflow designer, self-service rules engine, self-service reporting). Lead cloud cost efficiency initiatives, optimizing infrastructure, model execution, and compute resources. Collaborate closely with AWS Support and Solution Architects to optimize infrastructure and leverage cutting-edge cloud capabilities. Data & AI Infrastructure Architect high-scale, distributed data processing pipelines for batch and real-time workloads. Optimize data storage, retrieval, and processing layers to enhance system performance and reduce cost. Enable data self-service for analytics, ML, and real-time business use cases. Ensure data governance, security, and compliance across all systems. Technical Leadership & Hands-on Architecture Guide engineering teams on architectural best practices and pragmatic execution. Coach teams on scalable microservices, event-driven architectures, and cloud-native patterns. Practice "Architecting by Example" through technical prototyping and proof-of-concepts to validate architectural decisions. GenAI Acceleration & Architectural Advocacy You serve as the AI Adoption Catalyst and engineering champion, actively partnering with developers and business units to integrate LLMs and agentic workflows that securely hyper-automate the development lifecycle. You clear roadblocks and deploy agile architectural guardrails that empower teams to experiment rapidly with automated AI tools, building a self-service AI culture while maintaining rigorous cost-performance optimization. Your leadership evolves architectural governance into a collaborative platform for ensuring system-wide coherence, security, and world-class scalability. Architectural Governance & ARC Leadership Lead the Jumio Architecture Review Council (ARC) to drive cross-functional alignment and the evolution of our technical landscape. Establish and enforce architectural standards, ensuring consistency, security, and scalability across all product teams. Facilitate cross-team architectural reviews to identify technical debt, drive alignment, and ensure strategic coherence. Serve as the primary decision-maker for complex architectural trade-offs, balancing immediate delivery needs with long-term system health. Mentor engineering leadership on architectural best practices and standardized decision-making processes. Who You Are Strategic Visionary—you connect long-term business goals with robust technical roadmaps. Ultra-technical—you design, build, and optimize systems with a hands-on approach. System-First Thinker—you prioritize architecture, efficiency, and scale in every decision. Cloud-Native Expert—you utilize your deep AWS knowledge to optimize costs while improving system performance. Pragmatic Decision Maker—your impact-driven solutions ensure technical excellence without sacrificing speed. Builder’s Mentality—you thrive on automation, self-service, and reducing engineering toil through GenAI adoption. Growth-Oriented Mentor—you teach, coach, and elevate the engineering teams through architectural advocacy. Must-Have Skills & Experience 12+ years of hands-on experience in system architecture, data engineering, cloud engineering, or technical leadership roles. Experience with multi-tenant architectures and designing frameworks for configurable SaaS platforms. Deep, hands-on expertise in AWS (e.g., EKS, IAM, Lambda, networking) is required; professional experience with GCP is a strong plus. Strong experience with distributed systems, microservices, event-driven architectures, and caching strategies. Hands-on knowledge of AI/ML model execution—understanding model inference performance, cost trade-offs, and optimization strategies. Proficiency in high-scale transactional systems. Experience with infrastructure automation (Terraform, CI/CD, Kubernetes, Docker). Strong coding skills (Expert in Java, Strong in Python,  Knowledgeable in JavaScript/TypeScript & Kotlin). Strong experience leading architectural review processes and fostering engineering standards. Proven expertise in integrating GenAI and ML methodologies into the software development lifecycle. Proven ability in strategic stakeholder management and complex financial/TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) analysis for enterprise technology. Nice-to-Have Skills Experience with high-volume, real-time data processing and distributed streaming architectures. Experience building petabyte-scale distributed data platforms. Familiarity with fraud prevention, identity verification, or authentication technologies. Why Join Us? Impact at scale —we process millions of transactions and solve real-world security and identity challenges . Modern technical foundation with room to innovate —leverage our established, scalable cloud architecture while actively driving continuous modernization, operational cost optimization, and solving complex technical challenges. Hands-on architecture leadership —you won’t be stuck in meetings; you’ll drive execution. Work alongside top engineers and AI/ML experts , pushing the limits of what’s possible. Competitive compensation and high ownership —your work will define how Jumio scales. Jumio Values: IDEAL: Integrity, Diversity, Empowerment, Accountability, Leading Innovation Equal Opportunities : Jumio is a collaboration of people with different ideas, strengths, interests and cultures. We welcome applications and colleagues from all backgrounds and of all statuses. About Jumio: Jumio is a B2B technology company dedicated to eradicating online identity fraud, money laundering and other financial crimes to help make the internet safer. We leverage AI, biometrics, machine learning, liveness detection and automation to create solutions that are trusted by leading brands worldwide and respected by industry thought leaders. Jumio is the leading provider of online identity verification, eKYC and AML solutions. With a global footprint, we’re expanding the team to meet strong client demand across a range of industries including Financial Services, Travel, Sharing Economy, Fintech, Gaming, and others.
